item.title: COP31: Ambition goes missing as fossil fuel language drops from draft deal
item.description: A cat named Ambition went missing again at COP31 on Thursday. While activists delivered the message with humour, it reflected a serious concern: explicit references to moving away from fossil fuels had disappeared from the latest draft climate agreement. On the eve of the summit's scheduled close, ministers and the Presidency were still trying to bridge sharp differences as civil society groups pressed for stronger action.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: No government approval needed to form or join a group, UN rights committee says
item.description: People do not need their government’s permission to form or join an association, the UN Human Rights Committee said on Thursday, issuing new guidance as civic space shrinks around the world.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World’s top court finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya
item.description: The International Court of Justice, the principal judicial organ of the UN, delivered its judgment on Thursday in the case of The Gambia v. Myanmar on the application of the Genocide Convention, finding Myanmar responsible for the crime against the country’s ethnic Rohingya, the first such ruling against a State.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: COP31 deadlock persists as countries launch new ‘climate reality check’
item.description: With the clock running down at COP31 in Antalya, countries on Wednesday launched a new global check on whether climate promises are being kept, even as ministers remained deadlocked over some of the summit’s toughest questions: who pays, how fast the world moves away from fossil fuels and whether a greener future can be called “just” if poorer countries cannot afford it.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Patients running out of options as antibiotics stop working against common infections
item.description: Common bacteria are becoming highly resistant to front-line and even “last-resort” antibiotics, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) said on Wednesday, warning that the situation today is worse than it was in 2019.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Dozens more children killed in Yemen amid escalating hostilities
item.description: The UN child rights agency, UNICEF, on Wednesday called for warring parties in Yemen to protect children as renewed conflict between Houthi rebels and Government forces approaches the three-month mark.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Ukraine: Civilian casualties in 2026 already far exceed previous years’ tolls
item.description: This year has seen dramatically higher civilian casualties in Ukraine than any other year since the full-scale invasion of the eastern European country by Russia in February 2022, the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine (HRMMU) said on Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: Ebola cases double in DR Congo, chemical exposure starts before birth, Türk concern over EU-Rwanda transfer plan
item.description: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has more than doubled in three months, with more than 11,000 cases and 5,400 deaths now reported in 67 health zones across eight provinces, the head of the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: COP31: The push to protect warming oceans reaches the negotiating table
item.description: From identifying marine life with a cup of seawater to drawing on Indigenous knowledge to prevent wildfires, scientists and communities showcased both cutting-edge and time-tested ways to protect nature at COP31 on Tuesday. Yet turning innovation into action remains a challenge, with funding gaps persisting and ministers struggling to bridge divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance as negotiations enter their final days.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Haiti: ‘Atrocious abuses’ continue as UN warns anti-gang operations must priortise civilian protection
item.description: The UN human rights office, OHCHR has urged greater protection for civilians in Haiti amid ongoing “atrocious abuses” committed by gangs and intensified security operations.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Hunger should not be a concern’: WFP steps in for families in Kenya who fled Ethiopia violence
item.description: The World Food Programme (WFP) is assisting thousands of families who fled recent violence in Ethiopia for the Moyale area in neighbouring Kenya, the UN agency reported on Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Winter rains deepen Gaza crisis amid restricted access and aid cuts
item.description: Gaza is facing a deepening shelter, sanitation and food security crisis as winter rains flood makeshift shelters, destroy scarce food supplies and leave displaced families struggling to stay warm and fed.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Peace begins in our hearts’: Children close Muscat forum with a message to the world
item.description: Children from across the world sent a message of peace from the Omani capital Muscat on Monday, calling for an end to hatred, respect for diversity and the protection of human rights.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘An unfulfilled plan helps no one’: Superbug plans have doubled, but few countries are delivering
item.description: More countries are drawing up plans to tackle antimicrobial resistance (AMR), but major gaps in testing and treatment mean billions of people continue to be at risk, according to new data released by the World Health Organization (WHO) on Monday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Lebanon leading the way in mental health support
item.description: Mental health support must be a core part of the humanitarian response, said the UN Deputy Secretary-General during a visit to Lebanon over the weekend, where efforts to address the psychological toll of years of conflict and instability offer valuable lessons for other crisis-affected countries.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: AI gets climate science right – until users push back
item.description: The best AI models answer most climate science questions correctly, but they often abandon established facts as soon as a user disagrees, according to a new report co-authored by the UN.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Syria: Progress ‘real’ but fragile, as remnants of war wreck young lives
item.description: Syria is showing “undeniable signs of progress” nearly two years after the fall of the Assad regime, but explosive ordnance, the approaching winter and severe funding shortfalls threaten those fragile gains, senior UN officials told the Security Council on Monday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: COP31 enters decisive week as climate talks face political test and AI initiatives gather pace
item.description: New international initiatives on artificial intelligence and green industrialization showcased technology’s growing role in climate action, even as negotiators remained deadlocked on finance, fossil fuels and adaptation ahead of the final stretch of the UN talks.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Funding cuts raise risks of trafficking and exploitation for refugee children
item.description: Sharp reductions in humanitarian funding are putting refugees, particularly children, at increased risk of being trafficked, exploited or abused, while the systems that protect them are weakening.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Guterres calls for a legally binding instrument for ‘killer robots'
item.description: Talks began in Geneva on Monday to push for controls on lethal autonomous weapons systems that are often referred to as “killer robots”.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: At his final ASEAN Summit, Guterres upholds cooperation and action on Myanmar
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres underscored the need for stronger collaboration with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and an end to the crisis in Myanmar, in remarks to regional leaders meeting in the Philippine capital Manila on Monday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: First Person: Managing risk on Ukraine’s frontline
item.description: Humanitarian workers providing support to communities on the frontline of the war between Ukraine and Russia must balance remaining close to those in need with the heightened risks of operating in a warzone, according to the top UN official in Ukraine.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Empowering faith and Indigenous leaders to combat hate
item.description: Religious, traditional and Indigenous leaders need to be empowered to act as full partners in preventing conflict, not just praised for their role, speakers said Sunday at the opening of the Muscat Plan of Action Forum in Oman.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Nadia Murad: ‘Day by day, I took my story back’
item.description: Nobel Peace Prize laureate Nadia Murad has spent years telling the world about the atrocities committed against her and the Yazidi community by militants from the terrorist group, ISIL.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: When the rains fail: Preparing for drought in Central America
item.description: Across Central America’s so-called Dry Corridor, farming families live at the mercy of the rains. In southwestern Honduras, Anastacio Martínez Gómez has spent most of his 73 years learning to work the land. But experience can only take him so far.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Here, you can eat until you’re full’: Oleshky evacuees savour first proper meals in years
item.description: In a quiet hospital corridor in Kyiv, staff and volunteers push carts carrying steaming pots of chicken soup, bread and buckwheat porridge to patients recently evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky, in Ukraine’s southern Kherson region.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Security Council LIVE: Fragile Gulf calm tested as threats to Hormuz shipping mount
item.description: Nearly nine months after Israeli and US strikes on Iran set off a regional war, the Gulf remains on a knife edge. Iran has all but closed the Strait of Hormuz, which carried a fifth of the world’s oil before the conflict. Attacks on shipping are rising, and efforts to stop a return to full-scale fighting have yet to produce a deal. The Security Council is meeting at Bahrain’s request to discuss the threat to regional and maritime security. Follow live below – and for full meetings coverage year round, go here.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: COP31: Climate finance falls short as calls grow for polluters to pay
item.description: From emotional appeals for climate justice to high-stakes negotiations over billions of dollars, finance dominated discussions at COP31 on Friday. UN Secretary-General António Guterres warned that even tripling adaptation funding for vulnerable countries would meet less than a third of their needs, as pressure mounted on wealthy nations and major polluters to pay their fair share.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Lives are at stake’: Humanitarians call for swift entry of winter supplies in Gaza
item.description: Winter supplies must enter the Gaza Strip where “lives are at stake”, the UN and partners said in an urgent appeal on Friday, in the wake of deadly rainfall this past weekend.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: COP31: New initiative targets AI and reliable climate change information
item.description: New guidance has been issued to ensure that people everywhere can obtain credible climate change information from artificial intelligence (AI) and understand how the technology impacts the environment.
